column3: The Hebrew leaves the executing king unnamed and uses the image in his hand; BSB supplies Amaziah and uses in his grasp.
The Hebrew uses sons in both the introductory and quoted clauses; BSB uses sons first and children in the quotation. It ends with a passive putting to death, where BSB says each is to die.
The Hebrew leaves the victor unnamed and names collective Edom; BSB supplies Amaziah and uses Edomites.
The Hebrew says his heart lifted him; BSB says his heart became proud.
The Hebrew says each fled to his tents; BSB uses his home.
The Hebrew leaves the later traveler unnamed; BSB repeats Jehoash.
The Hebrew says the house of the king and sons of pledges; BSB uses royal palace and some hostages.
The Hebrew uses unnamed plural subjects and refers to Amaziah only by a pronoun; the BSB supplies “conspirators,” “Amaziah,” and “men,” and makes the sending passive.
The Hebrew expresses the burial passively; BSB says they buried him actively.
The Hebrew leaves both the builder and the deceased king unnamed; BSB supplies Azariah and Amaziah.
The Hebrew leaves the restorer unnamed and says by the hand of His servant; BSB supplies Jeroboam and uses through His servant.
The Hebrew explicitly says there was no one in each of the two groups; BSB describes both groups as afflicted.
The Hebrew says that the LORD had not spoken of blotting out Israel; BSB says that He had said He would not blot it out.
The Hebrew says to Judah in Israel; BSB says for Israel from Judah.
